# `k.rpc`

Import each declaration by name, for example `import k.rpc.Broadcast`.

| Declaration | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`Broadcast`](#broadcast) | Fans values out to subscribers by key, across requests and replicas (`docs/design/29-server-streaming.md`). |
| [`RemoteClient`](#remoteclient) | Builds a client of a protocol at an address known only at run time, such as a merchant's callback URL registered with the app (`docs/design/40-workspaces-and-services.md`). |
| [`RemoteService`](#remoteservice) | Where another service of the same system runs, and the secret its calls are signed with (`docs/design/40-workspaces-and-services.md`). |
| [`RpcFailure`](#rpcfailure) | A failure outside an rpc's handler, carried by the `rpcFailure` case every rpc error enum has (`docs/design/28-rpc-wire-format.md`, "Failures outside the handler"). |
| [`RpcOnlyError`](#rpconlyerror) | The error enum of an rpc with no errors of its own: `rpc featured() throws RpcOnlyError -> List<Product>`. |
| [`ServiceAuthenticated`](#serviceauthenticated) | The guard that admits only other services of the system (`docs/design/40-workspaces-and-services.md`): a call must carry a short-lived service token signed with the secret in [`ServiceConfig`](#serviceconfig), as a `remote` client sends it. |
| [`ServiceCaller`](#servicecaller) | The service that made the current call of an rpc guarded by [`ServiceAuthenticated`](#serviceauthenticated), as its verified service token names it (`docs/design/40-workspaces-and-services.md`). |
| [`ServiceConfig`](#serviceconfig) | The secret a serving app verifies service tokens with, for rpcs guarded by [`ServiceAuthenticated`](#serviceauthenticated) (`docs/design/40-workspaces-and-services.md`). |

## Broadcast

```k,ignore
@ServerOnly
public class Broadcast<Key, T> where Key implements Hashable, Key implements Codable, T implements Codable
```

Fans values out to subscribers by key, across requests and replicas
(`docs/design/29-server-streaming.md`). Held by a `@Scope(.server)`
service ([`k.core.ServiceScope.server`](k-core.md#servicescope)).

**Members**

- `init()`
  Creates a broadcast with no subscribers.
- `func publish(key: Key, value: T)`
  Delivers `value` to every current subscriber of `key`; inside a
  transaction, delivery waits for the app-level commit.
- `func subscribe(key: Key) -> Stream<T>`
  Subscribes to the values published for `key`.

  - Returns: a [`k.core.Stream`](k-core.md#stream) that starts receiving immediately
    and buffers values until they are read.

## RemoteClient

```k,ignore
@ServerOnly
public struct RemoteClient
```

Builds a client of a protocol at an address known only at run time,
such as a merchant's callback URL registered with the app
(`docs/design/40-workspaces-and-services.md`). The protocol is the
type the result is used as:
`let events: PaymentEvents = RemoteClient.at(url: hook, token: secret)`.
Calls go through the same codecs, timeouts and error mapping as a
`remote` rule's client ([`RemoteService`](#remoteservice)). Server-only.

**Members**

- `static func at<P>(url: Url, token: Secret<String>, timeout: Duration = 10.seconds) -> P`
  Builds a client of protocol `P`, the type the result is used as.

  - Parameters:
    - url: where the protocol is served.
    - token: the secret the calls are signed with.
    - timeout: how long to wait for each answer.
  - Returns: the client; failures outside the remote handler reach
    the caller as `rpcFailure` cases ([`RpcFailure`](#rpcfailure)).

## RemoteService

```k,ignore
public interface RemoteService
```

Where another service of the same system runs, and the secret its calls
are signed with (`docs/design/40-workspaces-and-services.md`). A
`config` implements it with `@Env` fields `url: Url` and
`token: Secret<String>`, and optionally `timeout: Duration` (10 seconds
when it has none); `use remote(Config) for Protocol` in `App.k` then
calls `Protocol` at that address, from the server only.

## RpcFailure

```k,ignore
public enum RpcFailure implements Error, Codable
```

A failure outside an rpc's handler, carried by the `rpcFailure` case
every rpc error enum has (`docs/design/28-rpc-wire-format.md`, "Failures
outside the handler"). Only the runtime produces it.

**Members**

- `case rejected(GuardRejection)`
  A guard refused the call; the payload says why.
- `case invalid(ValidationError)`
  A [`k.validation.Validatable`](k-validation.md#validatable) parameter failed validation.
- `case offline`
  The browser couldn't reach the server.
- `case timeout`
  The server didn't answer in time.

## RpcOnlyError

```k,ignore
public enum RpcOnlyError implements Error, Codable
```

The error enum of an rpc with no errors of its own:
`rpc featured() throws RpcOnlyError -> List<Product>`.

**Members**

- `case rpcFailure(RpcFailure)`
  A failure outside the handler ([`RpcFailure`](#rpcfailure)).

## ServiceAuthenticated

```k,ignore
@Guard
public struct ServiceAuthenticated
```

The guard that admits only other services of the system
(`docs/design/40-workspaces-and-services.md`): a call must carry a
short-lived service token signed with the secret in [`ServiceConfig`](#serviceconfig),
as a `remote` client sends it. A refused rpc throws
`rpcFailure(.rejected(.unauthenticated))`; the verified caller's name is
[`ServiceCaller.name`](#servicecaller).

## ServiceCaller

```k,ignore
@Scope(.app)
@ServerOnly
public service ServiceCaller
```

The service that made the current call of an rpc guarded by
[`ServiceAuthenticated`](#serviceauthenticated), as its verified service token names it
(`docs/design/40-workspaces-and-services.md`). Injected into the
service implementing the protocol; server-only.

**Members**

- `var name: String?`
  The calling app's `[package] name`; `nil` when the current request
  is not a verified service call.

## ServiceConfig

```k,ignore
public config ServiceConfig
```

The secret a serving app verifies service tokens with, for rpcs guarded
by [`ServiceAuthenticated`](#serviceauthenticated)
(`docs/design/40-workspaces-and-services.md`). It is the `token` of the
callers' [`RemoteService`](#remoteservice) configs. `k dev` at a
workspace root sets it, and the callers' tokens, to one generated
development secret.
